definition: Applying an objective to a chosen subset of tokens rather than uniformly, and across 5 sources the finest granularity at which the archive's methods intervene. The selection criteria differ and so do the arguments for them: divergence of a token's logit distribution from the group average rather than its entropy, on the argument that entropy marks uncertainty rather than distinctiveness; positions where a privileged teacher's distribution shifts most, which concentrate on reasoning-control and problem-conditioned state-update tokens while downweighting surface realisation; positions where the student almost never samples but the teacher prefers, which no on-policy update otherwise reaches; and marginal utility per token for pruning. Two findings recur. Which tokens are selected matters more than how many -- one sparsity ablation gives 66.23 pass@1 at a 10 percent selection against 63.37 at 20 percent, 60.62 for the bottom 90 percent of frequent tokens and 57.45 for uniform training. And the selected set is stable: overlap of the top-20 percent highest-entropy positions with the base model falls only from 100 to 86.67 percent over 1,360 training steps, so training largely preserves rather than installs the structure being selected on.

evidence.note: Concentrates privileged self-distillation on reasoning pivots identified by the teacher's distributional shift when an English reference solution is added or removed, for multilingual reasoning transfer.
evidence.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Defines a token's marginal utility as its log-probability gain for the ground-truth answer, then trains against negative-utility tokens to shorten chains of thought.
evidence.title: Think Better, Not Longer: Token-Level Marginal Utility for Efficient Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Prunes chain-of-thought segments the model's own likelihood landscape marks as extraneous, then trains on the resulting pruning preference pairs.
evidence.title: Your Reasoning Model Knows What Counts: Self-Guided Chain-of-Thought Pruning for Efficient Reasoning

evidence.note: Has a teacher decompose and prune a student's reasoning by mathematical skill, then distills the pruned paths back, on the argument that CoT structure must match student capacity.
evidence.title: DRP: Distilled Reasoning Pruning with Mathematical Skill-aware Step Decomposition for Efficient Large Reasoning Models

name: token selection
